This is a petition filed u/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

sentences.text:
The petitioner's case in brief:
That on 1962020 at about 6.30 a.m. when the petitioner was riding a scooter bearing No.KA05JL8443 Opp Bethal school U turn, BM road, Ramanagara town

,
at that time, rider of the scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585 JUDGMENT came from back side and hit the petitioner's vehicle, as a result of which petitioner sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
Immediately petitioner was shifted to Government hospital and later shifted to Ramakrishna hospital for further management and undergone surgery.
It is further stated that petitioner has spent more than Rs.2 lakhs towards medicine, treatment nourishing food and traveling expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and earning Rs.18,000/p.m. as agriculturist and dairy farming.

Due to accidental injuries,
petitioner is unable to do his work and suffering from severe pain and mental agony.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. The respondent No.1 remained absent and he placed exparte and respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel.

The second respondent filed written statement wherein contended that the alleged accident took place solely due to negligence of the petitioner himself who was riding the scooter without observing the movements of the vehicles on JUDGMENT the right, left and back side moving towards near and opposite to Bethal school U turn, BM road, Ramanagara town which said to be a busy and traffic road of and petitioner riding the said scooter in high speed without watching the movements of other opposite vehicles.
It is further contended that the petitioner was not having DL and insurance policy as on the date of accident.
It is contended that the insurance company has issued a policy of insurance in respect of the scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585 which is valid from 2211 2019 to 21112020.

The alleged accident as required u/s 134 (c) of the MV act like wise the jurisdictional police have not informed to this respondent as per Section 158 (6)
of the MV Act.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA05 JQ7585 on 1962020 at about 6.30 JUDGMENT a.m. at BM road, Opp Bethal school, U turn, Ramanagara town, Ramanagara ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and in her support P.W.2 is examined.
Exs.P1 to P12 documents are marked.

On the other hand respondents have not lead either oral or documentary Santhosha vs Naveen on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58225891/
2 evidence.
6.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. My answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following: REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of JUDGMENT the scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents as ExP1 to 10 i.e.,FIR, complaint, crime details form, spot sketch, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, Adhaar card, medical bills and discharge summary.
9.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sampreeth Kumar S/o Ramu, the Ramanagar police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed ExP7 charge sheet against the rider of scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585 for the offenses punishable under Sec's.279, 337, 338 of IPC, holding that accident in question has been taken place due to the the rash & negligent riding of scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. On Perusal of the cross examination by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance company goes to show that the factum of accident is not denied by it.

Only suggestions were made to the effect JUDGMENT that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not due to the negligence of the riding of the scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585 which were out rightly denied.
Under such circumstances oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence produced by the petitioner has to be accepted.
11. ExP5 wound certificate disclose that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
The aforementioned documentary evidence is not controverted by the respondents.
Hence there is no reason to disbelieve the same.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defense or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.

12. On perusal of EXP4Spot sketch it clearly shows that the accident has been taken place on the extreme left edge of the road which fortifies and strengthens the fact that when the petitioner was going by the side of the road, at that time, in Ramanagara town, BM road, Bethal school cross, rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA05JQ7585 came JUDGMENT from the back side of the petitioner and while over taking the petitioner vehicle from the left side touch the handle of the scooter of the petitioner and as a result of which both of them fell down and petitioner sustained fracture injuries to his right leg.

Further ExP4 reveals that there are sufficient space on the other side of the road for the rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA05JQ7585 to over take and these documents are not at all disputed by the respondents.

Even the respondent has not examined the Santhosha vs Naveen on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58225891/
3 rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA05JQ7585 to disprove the evidence given by the PW1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA05 JQ7585 has to state the facts and the circumstances which caused the accident.
But the rider of the scooter bearing reg.No.KA05JQ 7585 has not been examined.
13. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the rider of the scooter JUDGMENT bearing reg.No.KA05JQ 7585.
14.

Even otherwise, it is a settled law that in a claim petition, the claimant need not prove the happening of events beyond reasonable doubt and the rule of preponderance of probability would apply in such cases.

In the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others), it has been held that in a Road accident, the strict principles of proof as in a Criminal case are not attracted.

entities.text: AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relevant portion of the said decision is reproduced as follows:
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular Bus, in a particular manner, may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of Proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
JUDGMENT 15.
The point that merits consideration is that the degree of proof required for proving the negligence on the part of the rider of scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585.
In the present proceedings, is not as vigorous as is laid in proving the guilt of the accused in criminal trial.

The intent of the Motor Vehicles Act is benevolent and the entire purpose of the Legislation is likely to be defeated if in each case the petitioner is asked to prove the involvement and negligence on the part of the driver beyond reasonable doubt.

16. Therefore by applying the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the decisions cited supra, to the facts of the instant proceedings, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the rider of scooter bearing No.KA05JQ 7585 on account of his rash & negligent riding.
Hence issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.2 : As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the JUDGMENT actionable negligence of the rider of scooter bearing No.KA 05JQ7585.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 33 years.

The petitioner has produced the Aadhar Santhosha vs Naveen on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58225891/
4 card as per Ex.P.8, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 151986 and the accident took place on 1962020.

sentences.text: So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 34 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was Agriculturist and Dairy farming and earning Rs.18,000/p.m.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of her work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/ p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
19. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY: JUDGMENT

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : i.e., (1) abrasions over face/forehead (2)
abrasions over both forearms/knees (3) bimalleolar fracture right ankle with subluxation.
The doctor has mentioned in the wound certificate that the said injuries are fresh and grievous in nature.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P10discharge summary discloses that for the aforesaid injuries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Ramakrishna hospital Ramanagara from 1962020 to 2162020 for total period of 3 days and underwent surgeries i.e., ORIF with CC screws for the medial malleolus and plating for the fibula.
20.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.
Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 who stated that petitioner had sustained right ankle bimalleolar fracture with ankle subluxation.

PW2 doctor in his affidavit stated that as per the copy of discharge summary the petitioner was treated at Ramakrishna hospital JUDGMENT with ORIF with CC screws for the medial malleolus and plating for the fibula on 1962020 and discharged on 216 2020 and petitioner was on regular followup in the same hospital and fractures untied.

PW2 further stated that petitioner complains of weakness and pain in the right ankle unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and on examination petitioner has swollen right ankle and restricted right ankle movements.
PW2 further stated that recent xray of the right ankle shows untied fracture with implant in situ.
Further PW2 stated that sustained physical disability of right lower limbs at 35% and for wholebody at 12%.
PW2 in his cross examination has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and he has not given further treatment.
21. From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case JUDGMENT reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another.
22.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner being Agriculturist and dairy farming can do work with some disability.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 10%.

As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of above 34 age is '16'.

sentences.text: This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/ p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,88,000/ (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 16 X 10/100) which is rounded off to Rs.2,88,000/ is awarded under this head.

23. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained JUDGMENT the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained abrasion injuries and right ankle bimalleolar fracture with ankle subluxation and he has taken the treatment as inpatient for 3 days and undergone operations.

The petitioner has stated that inspite of the best available treatment, he has not come to normal position and due to the fracture injuries of his leg, petitioner is completely,
permanently disabled and suffering from deformity and injuries are not properly cured and he has to undergo one more surgery.
Hence petitioner is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 34 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.
24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:

By JUDGMENT considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 3 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner it is quite natural that he could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.60,000/ (15,000 X 4) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
25. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is residing in Malavalli Taluk and Mandya district and have treatment at Ramnagar as inpatient and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 3 days and undergone surgery and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his JUDGMENT treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/ is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: MEDICAL EXPENSES.
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.11 i.e.,medical bills and ExP9prescriptions for Rs.80,000/.
The respondents have not disputed the said medical bills, except denial suggestion.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to JUDGMENT award Rs.80,000/ under the head of medical expenses.
28. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : PW2 doctor has stated that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.50,000/.
The petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 3 times and undergone three operations.

Hence by considering the say of the doctor and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and future medical expenses required to the petitioner and also for other incidental charges i.e., for traveling expenses, food and other charges, this tribunal awarding Rs.60,000/ under the head future medical expenses.

29. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 15,00000 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 50,00000 3 Loss of income during laid : 60,00000 up period 4 Loss of future income due : 2,88,00000 to disability 5 Loss of future amenities & :
25,00000 happiness 6
Medical expenses : 80,00000 7

Future medical expenses :
60,00000 Total Rs.5,78,00000 JUDGMENT 30. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
31. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending scooter bearing No.KA05JQ7585 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
32. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
JUDGMENT O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,78,00000 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Santhosha vs Naveen on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58225891/
7
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
